name: Question 7
problem:
$$
[T]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}],\,{P}_{C\to B}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $[T]_{C}$ of a linear transformation $T$ with respect to the basis $C$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ shown above. Find the matrix of $T$ relative to the basis $B.$
worked_solution:
The connection between the matrices of our linear transformation $T$ relative to the bases $B$ and $C$ is given by the following diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067267/assets/2e82c232614bec8a98f079ea56d7913ee13e7b457e33e418198278d2e369fc5c.png)

Here, moving along an arrow means pre-multiplying by the corresponding matrix. Algebraically, we can write this as

$$
[T]_{C}={P}_{C\to B}^{-1}\cdot [T]_{B}\cdot {P}_{C\to B}.
$$

where ${P}_{C\to B}$ is the change-of-coordinates matrix from $C$ to $B.$

Our goal is to compute $[T]_{B}.$ Solving this equation for $[T]_{B},$ we obtain the alternative formulation

$$
[T]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}\cdot [T]_{C}\cdot {P}_{C\to B}^{-1}.
$$

First, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{C\to B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B}^{-1} & ={[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\cdot 3-2\cdot 4}[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can compute the matrix of $T$ relative to the basis $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[T]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}\cdot [T]_{C}\cdot {P}_{C\to B}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 8 \\ -8 & 11\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

[T]C=[2−4−23],PC→B=[3423]

Consider the matrix [T]C of a linear transformation T with respect to the basis C and the change-of-coordinates matrix PC→B shown above. Find the matrix of T relative to the basis B.

a
[−2−401]
b
[−68−811]
c
[−6−8−4−5]
d
[−6−16411]
e
[14−20−1217]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The connection between the matrices of our linear transformation T relative to the bases B and C is given by the following diagram:

Here, moving along an arrow means pre-multiplying by the corresponding matrix. Algebraically, we can write this as

[T]C=PC→B−1⋅[T]B⋅PC→B.

where PC→B is the change-of-coordinates matrix from C to B.

Our goal is to compute [T]B. Solving this equation for [T]B, we obtain the alternative formulation

[T]B=PC→B⋅[T]C⋅PC→B−1.

First, we compute the inverse of PC→B:

PC→B−1=[3423]−1=13⋅3−2⋅4[3−4−23]=[3−4−23]

Now, we can compute the matrix of T relative to the basis C:

[T]B=PC→B⋅[T]C⋅PC→B−1=[3423][2−4−23][3−4−23]=[−20−21][3−4−23]=[−68−811]
